title: Charlie Barnet in Hollywood
summary: Pecora rehearsed with Barnet around 1938-39 and says he was a nice, good-looking man whose wild image was publicity.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Did you ever know him? Oh, yeah.
Uh, I rehearsed with Charlie Barnett a couple of times, but Charlie couldn't get no work in Hollywood, see?

But I rehearsed with him, and, uh, I know Charlie a long time. Let's see. Uh, I met Charlie in 38, 39 somewhere. And he had, he was in a rehearsing band, but never to get anywhere. I don't know why, but...
Was he a character, or was that just publicity that they used to put out? And did he...
No, uh, Dick, I think, uh, Charlie's a nice guy. You know, uh, Charlie ain't a wild guy, nothing like that. He's not a wild guy. No.
That was just what they, they used to get those publicity men.
Well, he was, I tell you, he was a good-looking guy. Yeah. He took, uh, a lot of good movie stars out. Yeah.
He was rich, huh? Yeah, these folks had plenty of money.
Yeah, well, I mean, yeah, but that's, that's nothing. You know, they used to take pictures up to the swimming pool.
Well, everybody goes out with women, I mean, what the hell. Yeah, well... You ain't gonna sit home and look at radio.
No. Well, now we do. Now that we got all this gray hair, we do that.
